- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.

- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

"""Core cost aggregation helpers for Meridian billing tools."""

from collections import defaultdict


def monthly_total(rows):
    """Sum the ``amount`` of every row, grouped by its ``month`` key.

    ``rows`` is an iterable of mappings with a ``month`` string (e.g. ``"2026-01"``)
    and a numeric ``amount``. Returns a dict mapping month -> total amount.
    """
    totals = defaultdict(float)
    for row in rows:
        totals[row["month"]] += row["amount"]
    return dict(totals)

from .core import monthly_total

__all__ = ["monthly_total"]
__version__ = "0.3.1"

requires = ["setuptools>=61"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "costmap"
version = "0.3.1"
description = "Monthly and per-bucket cost summaries for Meridian billing tools"
requires-python = ">=3.9"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Meridian costmap — open a pull request from the current working-tree changes.
# Cuts a PR branch, commits the pending change, runs the test suite, and records the result.
# A successful run writes /var/log/meridian/pr.ok.
set -euo pipefail

REPO=/testbed
LOG_DIR=/var/log/meridian
TITLE="${1:-chore: update costmap}"
SLUG=$(printf '%s' "$TITLE" | tr '[:upper:] ' '[:lower:]-' | tr -cd 'a-z0-9-' | cut -c1-40)
BRANCH="pr/${SLUG:-update}"

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
cd "$REPO"

log() { echo "[pr] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/prepare.log"; }

log "stage 1/3: branch    $BRANCH"
git checkout -q -B "$BRANCH"

git add -A
git commit -qm "$TITLE" || true
log "stage 2/3: commit    $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

log "stage 3/3: test"
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_*.py' 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/prepare.log"

log "PR READY on $BRANCH"
date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ pr ready" > "$LOG_DIR/pr.ok"

# costmap development

The local script scripts/ci-sync.sh fetches and fast-forwards the current checkout from its local origin. scripts/prepare-pr.sh creates a pr/ branch, commits pending changes and runs the standard-library tests. The uncommitted bucket helper is the pending PR change. There are no external remotes.
